1. WARNING LABWARE-FOR-TECHNIQUE: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is
  a flat plate, and qPCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
   line 74:  p20.dispense(10, dest_well)
   The plate map says the technique is qPCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as
     its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3,
     load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is
     drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the
     reaction can never be run. The plate map checks what each well holds, not what plate it
     is.
   Affected: wells A1, A10, A11, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and 73 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips
     on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is qPCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. The plate map checks what each well holds, not what plate it is.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

protocol.py: 9 biology problems (6 errors, 3 warnings).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from tube A2 in slot 2: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 75:  p20.aspirate(1, fwd_dict[str(gene)])
   At line 75 the p20_single_gen2 draws 1 ul from fwd 1 (tube A2 in slot 2) with its tip 1
   mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 4 ul, which in this Opentrons 24
   Tube Rack with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap reaches only 0.89 mm up: the tip is above the liquid
   and draws air (this line did it 3 times, after 23 times in the liquid; 3 ul of air in
   all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 3 wells filled
   from these draws got air instead of liquid. Source wells: tubes A2, A3 and A4 in slot 2.
   Affected: tubes A2, A3 and A4 in slot 2.
   Also reached 3 other wells: wells C7, F10 and H3 in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 6 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
